summary: Lesson 2 (Make a Loonie) clears the high bar across all six categories. F1.1 is faithfully addressed and the expanded_walkthrough explicitly bridges to Lesson 1 (two 50-cent stacks forward-link) and forward to Lessons 3-5, making alignment a clean Level 4. Pedagogical depth is research-grounded: the trap is target-monitoring failure on Carpenter & Moser CGI 'join-result-unknown' chains with a Sowder 1992 citation on quantitative units, and recovery_moves branch into three named diagnostics (A: counts past 100 -> running-total target-monitoring drill; B: stops short -> fingers-as-dimes rebuild; C: only one route -> hide canonical 4-quarter solution). Instructional balance is Level 4 because Tappy/Lou puppets are explicitly OPTIONAL with named substitutes, materials are everyday paper coin cards/strips/anchor chart, the 12/25/13 split fits Grade 2 (50 min total), and a NO-MATERIALS PATH (10 fingers as 10 dimes; tap carpet 4x for quarters) is named in differentiation. Clarity_voice is anchored by Loonie Lou's quotable refrain 'One hundred cents, ONE LOONIE LOU!' echoed in the exit_routine cheer plus the unit refrain 'SAME AMOUNT - MANY WAYS! TAP TO PAY!'; all success_criteria use 'I can'; vocabulary has child-friendly definitions inherited from the blueprint. Mathematical_authenticity hits Level 4 because equivalence is framed conceptually (same value, different combo), Step 6 STRATEGY COMPARE has children share and compare combos by fewest/most coins with explicit CGI part-whole composition citation, and Lou's framing 'the MATH cares about the TOTAL' captures the equivalence principle precisely. Lesson_worksheet_consistency is Level 4: Parts 1 and 2 practise success criteria taught in the lesson (build $1, verify totals), and Part 3 (only nickels -> 20 nickels) is a deliberate transfer task that varies format from the lesson to verify generalisation to a non-canonical denomination. No revisions required.
